conclusions.statement: duhow builds and boots a custom /usr image, so its HTTP, MQTT and Dropbear capabilities are not stock QVCloud contracts.
The custom boot can run Sofia temporarily for hardware initialization and then stop NTS, which is not evidence of an active stock cloud path.
The Polish articles document WayFi with Hi3518EV200 and firmware V500.R001.A003.00.CG0021.B003, not Wi-Box F03266.

refs: Pasted U-Boot and Linux boot log

conclusions.statement: Only limited UART command meaning correlation is established between the WayFi CGI narrative and duhow code, without transferring the serial device or platform.
cmos486 implements an RTSP ONVIF PCMA sendonly backchannel, while go2rtc and the HA card provide the WebRTC browser path. The daemon is not shown to be a native WebRTC server.
RTSP, MQTT events, snapshots, OTA logic and Prometheus endpoints exist in the pinned custom source, but none was executed or tested on hardware.
The OTA code exists, but the packaged repository setting points to segator while FORK.md documents a device-level change to cmos486. MD5 is not an origin signature.
wibox-intercom-video-card is a Lovelace frontend requiring custom firmware and go2rtc, not a daemon or a stock integration.
segator replaces the vendor workflow with a custom local SIP media daemon and related MQTT, RTSP, snapshot, OTA and Prometheus functions. It does not prove stock SIP.
cmos486 and segator diverge at a55b8de, with 29 and 3 unique commits respectively. Later segator code aborts on TLS hostname setup failure while pinned cmos486 logs and continues.
The ESP32 project is a timed relay and HTTP/Telegram bridge for an unspecified Fermax intercom, with no demonstrated Wi-Box or cloud integration.
Recon and TROOPERS describe DUOX PLUS two-wire and RFID research. They do not establish Wi-Box, VDS or QVCloud behavior.

refs: General event and archive context only

conclusions.statement: The requested forum post /7 is an unverified user reliability narrative. The custom segator announcement is in /8 and remains community corroboration only.
F03266 is an officially documented VDS Wi-Box reference 3266, currently marked discontinued, with app features but no published protocol specification.
No custom capability was executed, so static source presence does not change runtime compatibility or any stock media, event or action status.

future_provider_implications.opportunity: A separately versioned local duhow profile for commands and events.
requirements: Custom duhow firmware and exact device/firmware identification
Explicit broker, topics, payloads and Home Assistant discovery contract
Authentication, transport security suitable for the deployment and secret handling
Reconnect, duplicate, gap, command correlation and physical acknowledgement tests
limitations: Plain MQTT and no physical acknowledgement in reviewed evidence
Not the static OAuth MQTT of the APK and not stock QVCloud

future_provider_implications.opportunity: Separate cmos486 or segator profiles for native MQTT entities and events, with media negotiated outside MQTT.
requirements: Choose one fork and commit instead of merging their contracts
Map media/state, UART events, snapshots and OTA entities explicitly
Validate SIP or RTSP separately and go2rtc/WebRTC only for cmos486
Test authentication, reconnection, duplicates and per-device capabilities
limitations: Different topics and semantics from duhow
No stock P2P or stock local MQTT evidence

future_provider_implications.opportunity: A versioned self-hosted API informed by the local HA architecture, without treating HA or go2rtc as a ready-made cloud.
requirements: Accounts, enrollment, inventory and authorization
Versioned events, actions, acknowledgement, media and recovery contracts
Revocation, secret storage, multi-user isolation and security tests
A concrete provider implementation before advertising any capability
limitations: No self-hosted adapter or API exists in this supplement
A relay cannot transparently certify QVCloud compatibility

future_provider_implications.opportunity: Expose real provider metadata, capabilities, events and actions to authorized Android clients while retaining provider-neutral boundaries.
requirements: A real provider with per-device capabilities before exposing an operation
UID and signing-certificate authorization, scopes and revocable grants
Ack levels, event gaps, cancellation, correlation and two-signature tests
A separate authorized channel for any future media, never large media parcels or secrets over Binder
limitations: Binder does not create provider compatibility
The reviewed external API design excludes media and secrets
